display.title: Episode 164: Three Lost on an Island, Chapter 1 (Rosh Chodesh Adar)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi takes children on a trip to Olam Haba with the pasuk Kol Yisroel, a class says the Shema, and a new story begins: three shipwreck survivors on a deserted island.
display.summary_long: Uncle Yossi opens with a journey further than outer space: to Olam Haba, the world to come. Our Sages teach that a lifetime of pleasure cannot equal one moment of the soul's joy there, and every Jew has a share reserved for him, as the Gemara in Sanhedrin says. This is Kol Yisroel, number four of the Twelve Pesukim, which the Hakochainik march then sings. After a sponsor message, Mitzvah Time features a listener reading her composition about achdus in her class. Story time begins 'Three Lost on an Island': after a storm sinks their ship, a doctor, a scientist and an engineer reach a deserted island. The doctor finds a rare healing apple, the scientist builds a telescope, and the engineer repairs an old airplane. Between the two halves of the story, a whole class from a Brooklyn girls' school recites the Shema. The chapter ends as all three look through the telescope at an amazing sight, to be revealed next week. Uncle Yossi closes with Mishenichnas Adar marbim b'simchah, since Rosh Chodesh Adar begins the next night, and three reasons every Jew has to be happy.
display.lesson: Every Jew has a place waiting in Olam Haba, earned through Torah and mitzvos; and when Adar comes we add more and more simchah.

date.note: Said on air: 'tomorrow night is Rosh Chodesh Adar' (eve of 30 Shevat 5745 = Wed 20 Feb 1985); shows aired Tuesdays. Weekly estimate (12 Mar) was 3 weeks late.

advisories.note: A ship sinks in a storm and only three people survive, stranded on a deserted island.

sources_cited.note: Kol Yisroel yesh lahem chelek l'Olam Haba.
